notes: Signing back in is now one tap: the app remembers the employee code and password you last signed in with, so after signing out both are already filled in and you just press Sign in. They are kept in the phone's own secure keystore, encrypted by Android, rather than in ordinary app storage — so keep your phone's screen lock on, because anyone who can unlock the phone can now sign in as you. If your password is changed or reset, the app forgets the old one instead of filling in something that no longer works. Attendance regularization can now carry a monthly limit. Where the company sets one, the screen tells you how many corrections you have left before you fill anything in. The count is against the month you are correcting, so filing late for last month does not spend this month's allowance, and a request that was rejected costs you nothing. If you have run out, HR can still raise the correction for you. Alongside this build, on the web: the regularization Approval setup screen — who signs off whose corrections, and the monthly limit itself — can now be given to an HR by a Super Admin on its own, without also handing over reporting lines and HR partners. One number covers the whole company, and a single person can be given a different one. Also, clicking a point on the joiners-vs-exits chart in Analytics now lists everyone for that month, instead of only the line you happened to click.
